steps.instructions: After correcting identified external issues, repeat the complete manufacturer-approved pre-use check. Do not return the ventilator to service because only one portion appears functional. Expected outcome: The complete pre-use check finishes successfully without faults.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm normal startup, ventilation using an appropriate test lung, displayed pressure and volume response, gas operation, controls, and audible and visual alarms as applicable. Expected outcome: The ventilator operates consistently and passes required return-to-service testing. If all results are acceptable, troubleshooting is complete.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Failure
steps.instructions: If the pre-use check continues to fail after external causes are ruled out, stop troubleshooting at the external level. Expected outcome: An unresolved ventilator is prevented from returning to clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Servo-c repeatedly failed its pre-use check before patient use.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the expiratory cassette was not fully seated, causing the pre-use check to fail.
CCR.Resolution: The cassette was correctly reseated, the complete pre-use check passed, and ventilator function and alarms were verified before return to service.

helpfulDetails: Stage of the check that failed

title: Getinge Servo-c Ventilator - Touchscreen or Control Input Unresponsive
description: Touchscreen or control inputs respond slowly, intermittently, or not at all because of contamination, physical damage, startup issues, or internal control-system faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Ventilation
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot unresponsive controls while a patient depends on the ventilator. Inability to change settings or respond to alarms can make the device unsafe even if ventilation currently continues. Move the patient to another verified ventilator before further testing. Expected outcome: The patient is supported by equipment with reliable controls.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Controls Are Affected
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves: Entire touchscreen Specific screen areas Physical controls Delayed response Intermittent response Frozen display with no control response Record whether displayed waveforms or values continue updating. Expected outcome: The control failure is clearly characterized.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Screen and Control Surface
steps.instructions: Check for moisture, cleaning residue, contamination, protective film problems, cracked glass, impact damage, or anything physically interfering with normal operation. Clean only using approved methods. Expected outcome: The external user interface is clean, dry, and free of obvious obstruction or damage. If responsiveness returns and remains stable, continue to functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify Basic Power Stability
steps.instructions: Confirm the ventilator is connected to known-good AC power and is not repeatedly transitioning between power sources. Observe for unexpected restarts, display flicker, or other symptoms suggesting unstable power. Expected outcome: Power is stable and unrelated power problems are ruled out.

steps.title: 5. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: With the ventilator removed from patient care, perform a normal shutdown and restart using approved operating controls. Do not force power interruption unless manufacturer documentation specifically permits it. Expected outcome: The ventilator boots normally and controls respond consistently. If normal function returns, continue testing for recurrence before returning to service.

steps.title: 6. Check All Normal User Inputs
steps.instructions: Verify the touchscreen and accessible physical controls respond across their intended operating functions without entering restricted service menus. Expected outcome: Control response is consistent and repeatable.

steps.title: 7. Run the Pre-Use Check
steps.instructions: Perform the complete manufacturer-approved pre-use check after restart. Expected outcome: The ventilator completes testing without control or display faults.

steps.title: 8. Perform Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Using a test lung, verify that settings can be entered, confirmed, and changed normally and that displayed information updates appropriately. Confirm alarms can be acknowledged through normal controls. Expected outcome: The user interface functions reliably throughout normal ventilator operation.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Intermittent or Persistent Failure
steps.instructions: If any touchscreen region or physical control remains intermittent, unresponsive, or unreliable, remove the ventilator from service even if a restart temporarily restores operation. Expected outcome: A ventilator with unreliable user controls is not returned to patient care.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Servo-c touchscreen did not consistently respond to selections.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried cleaning residue across the touchscreen surface interfering with reliable touch input.
CCR.Resolution: The screen was cleaned using the approved method, touch response was verified across normal operating functions, and the ventilator passed pre-use and functional testing.

title: Getinge Servo-air Ventilator - Alarm Speaker or Audible Alarm Failure
description: Addresses absent, weak, distorted, or intermittent audible alarms caused by settings, obstruction, environmental factors, or internal alarm-system faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Alarm Coverage
steps.instructions: A ventilator without reliable audible alarms must not remain the sole patient-support device. Move the patient to another verified ventilator or establish an appropriate alternate alarm and ventilation arrangement before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient monitoring does not depend on a questionable alarm speaker.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Audible Alarm Problem
steps.instructions: Using an approved controlled test condition, trigger an alarm that should produce an audible indication. Determine whether sound is absent, unusually weak, distorted, or intermittent. Expected outcome: The alarm speaker problem is reproduced and characterized.

steps.title: 3. Verify Alarm Audio Settings
steps.instructions: Review normal user-accessible alarm-volume settings and confirm they are not intentionally reduced or configured in a way that explains the complaint. Do not use restricted service menus to bypass alarm requirements. Expected outcome: Alarm audio is configured appropriately. If correcting an accessible setting restores normal sound, repeat alarm verification and stop troubleshooting when successful.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Speaker Area
steps.instructions: Inspect externally accessible speaker openings for tape, labels, packaging, debris, fluid residue, or another physical obstruction. Do not insert tools into the speaker opening. Expected outcome: The speaker opening is unobstructed and externally intact.

steps.title: 5. Evaluate Environmental Factors
steps.instructions: Test the alarm in a normal quiet bench environment to distinguish a true speaker failure from excessive ambient noise. Expected outcome: The audible alarm is clearly detectable under controlled conditions. If it is still weak or absent, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: 6. Perform a Normal Restart
steps.instructions: With the ventilator removed from patient service, shut down and restart normally. Repeat the controlled alarm test. Expected outcome: The audible alarm functions consistently following restart. A one-time recovery still requires sufficient testing to establish reliability.

steps.title: 7. Verify Multiple Alarm Conditions
steps.instructions: Create more than one safe, controlled alarm condition consistent with approved testing practices. Confirm audible annunciation occurs consistently and the visual alarm indication corresponds appropriately. Expected outcome: Audible alarms operate reliably across tested conditions. Troubleshooting can stop after completing required functional checks.

steps.title: 8. Check for Intermittent Audio
steps.instructions: Allow the unit to operate during bench testing and repeat alarm activation to identify intermittent loss, distortion, or fading. Expected outcome: Alarm sound remains stable. Any intermittent alarm-speaker function requires removal from service.

steps.title: 9. Complete Pre-Use and Alarm Verification
steps.instructions: Run the required pre-use check and applicable alarm testing before considering return to service. Expected outcome: Audible and visual alarms operate normally throughout testing.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Audible Alarm Failure
steps.instructions: If alarms remain absent, weak, distorted, or intermittent after external checks and normal restart, discontinue troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator remains out of service for internal alarm-system evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Servo-air displayed alarms but the audible alarm was difficult to hear.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external speaker opening partially covered by adhesive residue and a misplaced label.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed the obstruction, verified clear audible alarms under multiple test conditions, completed functional testing, and returned the ventilator to service.

helpfulDetails: Alarm sound absent, weak, distorted, or intermittent

title: Getinge Servo-air Ventilator - Battery Not Charging or Short Runtime
description: Addresses charging or runtime problems caused by AC supply, cord connection, battery seating, battery condition, storage, or charging-system faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Power
steps.instructions: If the ventilator is supporting a patient, connect it to reliable AC power when possible and arrange another verified ventilator before testing battery operation. Do not intentionally remove AC power from a patient-dependent ventilator with questionable battery capacity. Expected outcome: Patient ventilation is protected from unexpected power loss.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Battery Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue is: Battery not charging Battery not recognized Unexpectedly short runtime Rapidly falling battery indication Ventilator shutting down during battery operation Note the battery status indications. Expected outcome: The specific battery symptom is identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify AC Power
steps.instructions: Confirm the power cord is fully connected to the ventilator and a known-good outlet. Test the outlet with an appropriate device if necessary. Inspect the power cord, plug, and external inlet for damage. Expected outcome: Reliable AC power reaches the ventilator and normal AC operation is indicated. If charging resumes, continue monitoring and verify battery condition before return to service.

steps.title: 4. Allow Normal Charging Opportunity
steps.instructions: If the battery has been deeply discharged or the device has been stored, connect the ventilator to reliable AC power and allow charging according to applicable manufacturer guidance. Do not assume battery failure from a brief charging period. Expected outcome: The battery charge indication progresses normally. If charging remains absent, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Battery Installation
steps.instructions: Where accessible through normal approved handling, verify the battery is fully seated, latched, and free of obvious swelling, cracks, leakage, contamination, or terminal damage. Do not use a visibly damaged or swollen battery. Expected outcome: The battery is correctly installed and physically safe. Damaged batteries are removed from service according to facility battery-handling procedures.

steps.title: 6. Reseat the Battery
steps.instructions: Remove and reinstall the battery only if permitted by normal service handling and while patient care is protected. Expected outcome: The battery is recognized and charging normally. If reseating resolves the problem, complete runtime and functional verification before return to service.

steps.title: 7. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Battery
steps.instructions: Install a known-good approved battery when available. Expected outcome: If charging and runtime return to normal, the original battery is the likely cause and should be replaced. If the known-good battery also fails to charge, suspect a device-level charging issue and escalate.

steps.title: 8. Verify Battery Runtime
steps.instructions: After adequate charging, operate the ventilator on battery under an appropriate controlled test condition and evaluate runtime according to applicable manufacturer and department criteria. Expected outcome: Battery operation is stable and meets applicable acceptance criteria. Troubleshooting can stop if the battery passes.

steps.title: 9. Confirm Automatic Power Transition
steps.instructions: Verify the ventilator properly indicates AC operation and, during controlled testing, transfers appropriately between external and battery power. Expected outcome: Power transitions occur without unexpected shutdown or reset.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Charging Problems
steps.instructions: If a known-good battery will not charge or battery status remains abnormal despite verified AC input, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator remains out of service for charging-system evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Servo-air battery was not charging and the unit had very limited battery runtime.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the installed battery would not accept a normal charge, while a known-good battery charged correctly.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the defective battery, verified charging and battery operation, completed functional testing, and returned the ventilator to service.

title: Getinge Servo-air Ventilator - Expiratory Cassette Not Recognized or Not Seated
description: Addresses cassette recognition or seating problems caused by improper insertion, contamination, moisture, damage, incompatible components, or external obstruction.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: Do not remove, reseat, or troubleshoot the expiratory cassette while a patient depends on the ventilator. Move the patient to another verified ventilator or alternate ventilation method first. Expected outcome: The patient is safely supported and the affected ventilator is removed from active clinical use.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Power the Servo-air in a controlled test setting and verify whether the cassette is actually not recognized, will not seat, or produces a related startup or pre-use check failure. Note any displayed message without assuming an internal failure. Expected outcome: The exact cassette-related symptom is reproduced. If the problem cannot be reproduced, inspect carefully and complete full verification before considering return to service.

steps.title: 3. Remove and Inspect the Cassette
steps.instructions: Remove the expiratory cassette using normal approved handling. Inspect for: Cracks or broken housing Warping Contamination Excess moisture where it should not be present Damaged interfaces Foreign material Do not disassemble the cassette beyond approved handling. Expected outcome: The cassette is visibly intact and suitable for reinsertion. A damaged cassette should be replaced rather than forced into the ventilator.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Cassette Receptacle
steps.instructions: With the unit safely powered as appropriate for inspection, examine the external cassette mounting area for debris, fluid, bent external features, or an obstruction preventing full insertion. Do not probe internal contacts or disassemble the ventilator. Expected outcome: The receptacle is clean, unobstructed, and capable of accepting the cassette normally.

steps.title: 5. Reseat the Cassette
steps.instructions: Install the cassette evenly and completely without excessive force. Verify that it reaches its normal seated position. Do not force a cassette that binds or does not align normally. Expected outcome: The cassette seats securely and the ventilator recognizes it. If recognition is restored and subsequent pre-use testing passes, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Verify Cassette Compatibility and Processing Status
steps.instructions: Confirm the cassette is intended for the Servo-air and has been processed, cleaned, dried, and prepared according to facility and manufacturer requirements. A cassette that is still wet, improperly assembled after processing, or incompatible should not be used. Expected outcome: A compatible, correctly prepared cassette is installed.

steps.title: 7. Substitute a Known-Good Cassette
steps.instructions: Install a known-good compatible expiratory cassette when available. Expected outcome: If the known-good cassette is recognized normally, the original cassette is the likely external cause and should be removed from use. If neither cassette is recognized, stop repeated substitutions and escalate.

steps.title: 8. Repeat the Pre-Use Check
steps.instructions: Perform the complete required pre-use check after the cassette is properly recognized. Expected outcome: The cassette remains recognized and the ventilator completes the required checks. Troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 9. Escalate Persistent Recognition Failure
steps.instructions: If multiple known-good compatible cassettes fail to be recognized or cannot seat despite a clean and unobstructed receptacle, do not attempt deeper disassembly or adjustment. Expected outcome: The ventilator remains removed from service for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Servo-air would not recognize the expiratory cassette during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the installed cassette was not fully seated in the cassette receptacle.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed and correctly reinstalled the cassette, confirmed recognition, completed the pre-use check successfully, and returned the ventilator to service.

title: Getinge Servo-air Ventilator - High Airway Pressure Alarm
description: Addresses high-pressure alarms caused by tubing obstruction, water, filters, patient-interface issues, settings, expiratory restriction, or ventilator malfunction.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient First
steps.instructions: A high airway pressure alarm during clinical use can represent a patient, airway, or equipment emergency. Clinical personnel should immediately assess the patient and airway and provide alternate ventilation if adequate ventilation cannot be confirmed. Clinical Engineering should troubleshoot the device only after patient care is stabilized. Expected outcome: The patient is safely ventilated independently of any questionable equipment.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Whether the Alarm Is Device-Related
steps.instructions: Use an appropriate test lung after the ventilator is removed from the patient. Reproduce the operating configuration if safe and note when the high-pressure alarm occurs. Expected outcome: The alarm either reproduces on a test load, indicating an equipment/setup issue, or does not reproduce, suggesting the clinical circuit or patient condition may have contributed.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Breathing Circuit for Obstruction
steps.instructions: Check the inspiratory and expiratory limbs for: Kinks Pinched tubing Water accumulation Blocked connectors Obstructed filters Closed valves or caps Incorrect circuit assembly Expected outcome: The circuit is open and correctly assembled. If removing an obstruction eliminates the alarm, troubleshooting can stop after complete functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect Filters and Accessories
steps.instructions: Check bacterial/viral filters, HMEs, humidification components, nebulizer adapters, and other inline accessories for restriction or incorrect orientation. Substitute known-good compatible components where appropriate. Expected outcome: External accessories provide an unrestricted gas path. A restricted component that causes the alarm is replaced.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Expiratory Cassette
steps.instructions: Verify the expiratory cassette is correctly seated, clean, properly prepared, and free from obvious obstruction or damage. Expected outcome: Exhaled gas can pass through the expected expiratory path without obvious external restriction.

steps.title: 6. Verify Ventilator Settings
steps.instructions: Review the selected mode, pressure limits, PEEP, tidal volume or pressure targets, flow-related settings, and alarm settings as applicable. Do not alter clinical settings simply to silence the alarm. For bench testing, use an appropriate controlled configuration. Expected outcome: Settings are internally consistent with the intended test setup and are not causing an expected alarm response.

steps.title: 7. Test With a Simplified Known-Good Circuit
steps.instructions: Replace the patient circuit and external accessories with a known-good compatible test configuration. Expected outcome: The high-pressure alarm no longer occurs. Reintroduce components individually if necessary to locate an external restriction.

steps.title: 8. Check for Abnormal Ventilator Output
steps.instructions: Observe pressure response on an appropriate test lung and, when required, use approved ventilator test equipment. Listen for unusual turbine noise and observe for abnormal pressure rise that occurs despite an unrestricted circuit. Expected outcome: Pressure responds predictably to test conditions. Unexpected pressure behavior requires removal from service.

steps.title: 9. Verify Alarm Function
steps.instructions: After correcting the cause, intentionally create an appropriate controlled high-pressure condition using approved testing methods to confirm the alarm activates and clears correctly. Expected outcome: The alarm operates normally and ventilation resumes appropriately after the test condition is removed.

steps.title: 10. Escalate if the Alarm Persists
steps.instructions: If high pressure occurs with a known-good unrestricted circuit and appropriate test setup, discontinue external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator remains out of service for service-level evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported repeated high airway pressure alarms on the Servo-air during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a kinked expiratory circuit limb restricting gas flow.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the affected circuit, verified normal ventilation and high-pressure alarm operation with a test lung, completed the pre-use check, and returned the ventilator to service.

title: Getinge Servo-air Ventilator - Network, Serial, or Data Communication Failure
description: Addresses lost device communication caused by cables, ports, network infrastructure, interface equipment, configuration, or downstream system availability.

steps.title: 1. Protect Clinical Monitoring and Workflow
steps.instructions: If ventilator data is required at a central station, EMR, integration system, or remote monitoring location, confirm clinical staff have an alternate method to monitor and document the patient before troubleshooting. Do not allow a communication failure to create an unnoticed loss of clinical surveillance. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely despite the communication outage.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Communication Failure
steps.instructions: Determine exactly what is failing: Network connection Serial communication Device integration Central monitoring Data export Interface engine reception One-way or intermittent data flow Confirm whether local ventilator operation remains normal. Expected outcome: The communication path and scope of failure are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect External Communication Cables
steps.instructions: Check Ethernet, serial, interface, adapter, and other relevant external cables for secure connection, damage, bent connectors, strain, or improper routing. Reseat accessible connections. Expected outcome: Physical connections are secure. If communication returns and remains stable, troubleshooting can stop after end-to-end verification.

steps.title: 4. Check Link and Status Indicators
steps.instructions: Observe applicable port, adapter, network, or integration-device indicators. Compare with a functioning nearby system when useful. Expected outcome: Link indicators are consistent with a functioning connection. Missing link at both ends suggests a cable, port, or infrastructure issue.

steps.title: 5. Substitute a Known-Good Cable or Port
steps.instructions: When permitted, replace the external cable with a known-good equivalent or connect to a verified infrastructure port. Avoid changing network configuration simply to test connectivity. Expected outcome: Communication is restored with the known-good cable or port, identifying the external failed element.

steps.title: 6. Verify Normal Accessible Communication Configuration
steps.instructions: Review user-accessible network or communication configuration and compare it with the expected approved configuration or a known-good device. Do not alter protected addresses, integration parameters, or service-level settings without authorization. Expected outcome: Device communication settings match the intended environment.

steps.title: 7. Check the Downstream System
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the receiving system, bedside interface, device adapter, switch, serial converter, integration server, or clinical application is functioning for other devices. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to either the Servo-air side or the external infrastructure.

steps.title: 8. Perform an End-to-End Test
steps.instructions: After correcting any cable, port, or configuration issue, verify data at the actual intended destination rather than relying only on a local link indication. Expected outcome: Expected ventilator data reaches the receiving system consistently. Troubleshooting can stop after successful end-to-end verification.

steps.title: 9. Confirm Ventilator Operation Is Unaffected
steps.instructions: Run appropriate functional and pre-use checks to ensure communication troubleshooting did not affect normal ventilator configuration or operation. Expected outcome: Ventilation and alarms remain fully functional.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Unresolved Communication Failure
steps.instructions: If known-good cables, ports, infrastructure, and approved configuration have been verified but communication remains unavailable, escalate to the appropriate Clinical Engineering, IT, integration, or manufacturer support group. Expected outcome: The device is removed from the affected communication workflow until the complete path is restored and verified.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Servo-air was operating normally but no ventilator data appeared in the connected monitoring system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a damaged external network cable between the ventilator connection and the bedside interface.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the cable, verified data transmission at the receiving system, confirmed normal ventilator operation, and returned the device to service.

title: Getinge Servo-air Ventilator - O2 Cell Calibration Failure or Incorrect FiO2
description: Addresses oxygen calibration or FiO2 discrepancies caused by oxygen supply, circuit setup, sensor condition, configuration, leaks, or calibration-related problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: If delivered oxygen concentration is questionable, move the patient to another verified ventilator or maintain therapy with an appropriate alternate device. Do not troubleshoot questionable oxygen delivery while a patient depends on the ventilator. Expected outcome: The patient receives reliable oxygen therapy independently of the affected unit.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Oxygen Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue is a calibration failure, unstable oxygen reading, discrepancy between set and measured FiO2, or another oxygen-related message. Use an approved external oxygen analyzer when clinically or technically appropriate. Expected outcome: The oxygen discrepancy is confirmed or ruled out using an independent method.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Oxygen Source
steps.instructions: Inspect the oxygen hose and fittings for secure connection, damage, kinks, or leakage. Verify that the connected oxygen source is available and appropriate using an approved external method. Expected outcome: A reliable oxygen source is connected. If restoring the source resolves the problem, repeat calibration and functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Breathing Circuit
steps.instructions: Check for major leaks, disconnected tubing, incorrectly installed components, open ports, or other conditions that could affect oxygen delivery or measurement. Expected outcome: The patient circuit is complete and leak-free to the extent required for testing.

steps.title: 5. Confirm Relevant Settings and Configuration
steps.instructions: Review the intended oxygen setting and any normal user-accessible configuration affecting oxygen delivery. Do not enter unauthorized service menus or change protected calibration values. Expected outcome: The ventilator is configured as intended for the test condition.

steps.title: 6. Perform the Approved Oxygen Calibration
steps.instructions: With the ventilator configured correctly and a verified oxygen source available, perform the normal approved calibration procedure available to trained personnel. Do not bypass failed calibration or force acceptance of questionable values. Expected outcome: Calibration completes normally. If it succeeds and independent oxygen measurement is accurate and stable, troubleshooting can stop after final testing.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Replaceable Oxygen-Sensing Components
steps.instructions: If the installed oxygen-sensing component is externally accessible and approved for routine replacement, inspect it for age-related deterioration, contamination, loose installation, or obvious damage. Do not disassemble internal sensing assemblies. Expected outcome: The oxygen-sensing component is properly installed and appears serviceable.

steps.title: 8. Use a Known-Good Approved Component if Applicable
steps.instructions: Where the oxygen-sensing element is an approved replaceable item, substitute a known-good compatible component and repeat calibration. Expected outcome: Calibration and FiO2 measurement return to normal. Replace the defective sensing component and complete performance testing.

steps.title: 9. Verify FiO2 With Approved Test Equipment
steps.instructions: Operate the ventilator into an appropriate test load and compare delivered oxygen concentration with an approved calibrated oxygen analyzer. Expected outcome: Delivered and indicated oxygen performance are acceptable under applicable manufacturer and department criteria. Troubleshooting can stop when full verification is successful.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Oxygen Errors
steps.instructions: If calibration repeatedly fails or oxygen delivery remains inaccurate after verifying source, circuit, settings, and approved replaceable components, discontinue external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The unit stays out of service for qualified oxygen-system evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Servo-air failed oxygen calibration and displayed an FiO2 value inconsistent with the selected setting.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the oxygen supply hose was not fully connected to the source.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the oxygen connection, completed oxygen calibration successfully, verified delivered oxygen with an approved analyzer, and returned the ventilator to service.

title: Getinge Servo-air Ventilator - Patient Circuit Leak or Disconnection Alarm
description: Addresses leak or disconnection alarms caused by loose tubing, open ports, damaged circuits, humidification components, interfaces, or expiratory-system problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: If a leak or disconnection alarm occurs during ventilation, clinical staff should immediately confirm the patient connection and effective ventilation. If adequate ventilation is uncertain, use another verified ventilator or an appropriate alternate ventilation method before Clinical Engineering troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Reliable ventilation is maintained while the Servo-air is removed from patient dependence.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Alarm Condition
steps.instructions: Connect the ventilator to an appropriate test lung using the reported circuit configuration and determine whether the alarm can be reproduced. Expected outcome: The leak or disconnection condition is confirmed under controlled testing.

steps.title: 3. Inspect All Circuit Connections
steps.instructions: Trace the circuit from the ventilator to the patient connection point. Check every connection for looseness or incomplete engagement. Pay particular attention to adapters, elbows, humidifiers, filters, water traps, and extension tubing. Expected outcome: All circuit connections are secure. If reseating a loose connection eliminates the alarm, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 4. Check for Open Ports or Missing Caps
steps.instructions: Inspect sampling ports, nebulizer ports, drainage points, accessory ports, and test connectors for openings that should be closed in the current setup. Expected outcome: No unintended open pathway remains in the breathing circuit.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Tubing and Accessories for Damage
steps.instructions: Look for cracks, splits, loose cuffs, punctures, distorted connectors, or damaged seals. Flex suspect tubing gently while observing for an intermittent leak. Expected outcome: The circuit and accessories remain intact. Damaged components are replaced.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Humidification Components
steps.instructions: Verify the humidifier chamber and related connectors are properly installed and sealed. Check for incorrect seating or assembly that could create a significant leak. Expected outcome: Humidification components are correctly installed without obvious leakage.

steps.title: 7. Verify the Expiratory Cassette
steps.instructions: Confirm the expiratory cassette is fully seated and properly recognized. Inspect the external interface for obvious contamination or damage. Expected outcome: The expiratory cassette is correctly installed and does not contribute to the leak condition.

steps.title: 8. Substitute a Known-Good Circuit
steps.instructions: Install a known-good compatible breathing circuit and test lung. Expected outcome: If the alarm clears, the original circuit or accessory set contains the leak. Replace or isolate the defective external component.

steps.title: 9. Perform Leak and Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Run the required pre-use or circuit verification process and operate the ventilator on an appropriate test load. Confirm stable delivered and exhaled ventilation and normal alarm behavior. Expected outcome: No unexpected leak or disconnection alarm occurs. Troubleshooting can stop after successful verification.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Leak Detection
steps.instructions: If the alarm persists with a known-good sealed circuit and correctly seated cassette, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator remains out of service for evaluation of sensing, valves, pneumatic pathways, calibration, or other internal causes.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported a persistent patient circuit leak alarm on the Servo-air.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a loose humidifier-chamber connection creating a significant circuit leak.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reseated the humidifier connection, completed the circuit and pre-use checks, verified normal ventilation and alarm operation, and returned the ventilator to service.

title: Getinge Servo-air Ventilator - Pre-Use Check Failure
description: Addresses failed pre-use checks caused by circuit setup, expiratory cassette, accessories, gas supply, power, leaks, or other externally correctable conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove the Ventilator From Active Use
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot a ventilator while a patient depends on it. Transfer ventilation to another verified device or appropriate alternate ventilation method before troubleshooting. Inspect the ventilator for obvious damage, contamination, fluid intrusion, unusual odor, or evidence of overheating. Expected outcome: The patient is safely supported elsewhere and the Servo-air is available for controlled troubleshooting. If physical or electrical damage is present, remove the unit from service and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Pre-Use Check Failure
steps.instructions: Repeat or review the pre-use check only when the ventilator is configured safely for testing. Note the exact stage that fails and any displayed message. Determine whether the failure is repeatable or occurred only once. Expected outcome: The failed portion of the pre-use process is identified. If the check now completes normally after correcting an obvious setup issue, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 3. Verify AC Power and Basic Startup
steps.instructions: Confirm the AC power cord is fully seated and connected to a known-good outlet. Inspect the cord and plug for damage. Power the ventilator normally and verify that startup completes without abnormal resets or power indications. Expected outcome: The ventilator starts normally from reliable AC power. If normal power restores successful pre-use testing, troubleshooting can stop after completing the full verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Patient Circuit
steps.instructions: Verify that the intended patient circuit is correctly assembled and fully connected. Check for: Loose or disconnected tubing Cracked tubing or connectors Open accessory ports Incorrectly installed humidification components Missing plugs or caps required during testing Damaged test lung or other test accessory Reseat all external circuit connections. Expected outcome: The breathing circuit is complete, secure, and free of obvious leaks or damage. If correcting the circuit allows the pre-use check to pass, troubleshooting can stop after successful completion of the entire check.

steps.title: 5. Inspect and Reseat the Expiratory Cassette
steps.instructions: Confirm the expiratory cassette is the correct compatible component, clean, dry as required for use, undamaged, and fully seated. Remove and reinstall it according to normal approved handling procedures. Do not disassemble the cassette beyond permitted user/service handling. Expected outcome: The cassette seats securely and is recognized by the ventilator. If the pre-use check passes afterward, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Verify Oxygen Supply and External Connections
steps.instructions: If oxygen is required for the check, inspect the oxygen hose and source. Verify the hose is connected securely and is not kinked or visibly damaged. Confirm the facility source or approved test source is available using an appropriate external method. Expected outcome: Required oxygen supply is available and connected correctly. If restoring the supply permits the pre-use check to pass, troubleshooting can stop after complete verification.

steps.title: 7. Remove Nonessential Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect optional external accessories that are not required for the pre-use check and could affect circuit integrity or communication. Repeat the check using the simplest approved configuration. Expected outcome: The ventilator completes the check in the basic configuration. Reconnect accessories individually to identify an external contributor before returning the device to service.

steps.title: 8. Use Known-Good External Components
steps.instructions: When available, substitute known-good compatible components such as the patient circuit, expiratory cassette, test lung, oxygen hose, or other replaceable external accessory implicated by the failed check. Change one item at a time. Expected outcome: The failed condition follows a defective external component or disappears with a known-good substitute. Replace the defective component and stop troubleshooting after successful pre-use verification.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Run the complete required pre-use check again after corrections. Verify normal ventilation into an appropriate test load and confirm expected alarm indications and controls function. Expected outcome: The complete pre-use check passes without recurring faults and the ventilator operates normally. The unit may proceed to return-to-service evaluation according to department policy.

steps.title: 10. Escalate if the Pre-Use Check Still Fails
steps.instructions: If the same failure persists despite correct power, circuit, cassette, oxygen source, accessories, and known-good substitutions, discontinue external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator remains out of clinical use pending qualified bench evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Servo-air repeatedly failed its pre-use check before patient use.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a loose patient-circuit connection creating a leak during the pre-use check.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the circuit connection, repeated the complete pre-use check successfully, verified ventilation and alarms, and returned the ventilator to service.

helpfulDetails: Exact failed pre-use check stage or displayed message

title: Getinge Servo-air Ventilator - Touchscreen or Control Input Unresponsive
description: Addresses unresponsive touchscreen or controls caused by contamination, obstruction, startup state, power instability, accessories, or service-level control faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: If controls cannot be reliably operated during ventilation, move the patient to another verified ventilator or appropriate alternate ventilation method. Do not continue clinical use when settings or alarms cannot be reliably accessed. Expected outcome: Patient support does not depend on an unreliable control interface.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Input Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the entire touchscreen is unresponsive, only part of the screen fails to respond, a specific control is affected, or the interface is frozen. Observe whether displayed waveforms, clock, or other indicators continue updating. Expected outcome: The failure is characterized as localized input loss, complete interface freeze, or broader system problem.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Screen and Controls
steps.instructions: Check for moisture, gel, cleaning residue, tape, protective film, gloves or objects pressing against the screen, and visible physical damage. Clean the exterior according to approved procedures. Expected outcome: The screen and controls are clean, dry, unobstructed, and undamaged. If responsiveness returns, complete functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify Stable Power
steps.instructions: Confirm operation on a known-good AC source and inspect the power cord. Power instability can produce apparent interface problems or repeated resets. Expected outcome: The ventilator receives stable AC power without abnormal rebooting.

steps.title: 5. Perform a Normal Restart
steps.instructions: With the ventilator removed from patient use, perform a normal shutdown and restart using approved operating controls. Do not force undocumented resets or access unauthorized service functions. Expected outcome: The interface initializes and responds normally. If the problem clears, continue testing to confirm it does not recur.

steps.title: 6. Remove Nonessential External Connections
steps.instructions: Disconnect optional data, serial, USB, network, or other external accessories that are not required for basic operation. Restart and retest. Expected outcome: The touchscreen and controls remain responsive in a basic configuration. Reconnect accessories one at a time if an external device appears related.

steps.title: 7. Check for Intermittent or Localized Failure
steps.instructions: Test normal user-accessible controls across the display and observe for dead areas, delayed response, unintended activation, or intermittent freezing. Do not calibrate the touchscreen through undocumented or restricted menus. Expected outcome: All required controls respond consistently. Any persistent dead area or erratic activation requires removal from service.

steps.title: 8. Verify Alarm and Setting Interaction
steps.instructions: Using a safe test setup, confirm that settings can be selected and adjusted normally and that alarms can be acknowledged through the intended controls. Expected outcome: The operator interface supports reliable control of ventilation and alarms.

steps.title: 9. Complete Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Run the required pre-use check and verify the unit remains responsive throughout normal test operation. Expected outcome: Controls remain stable and responsive. Troubleshooting can stop if the issue does not recur.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Interface Failure
steps.instructions: If the touchscreen freezes, has dead areas, activates unpredictably, or remains unresponsive after basic external checks and a normal restart, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator remains out of service for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Servo-air touchscreen stopped responding during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried cleaning residue across the touchscreen causing unreliable touch response.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned and dried the touchscreen using the approved method, verified reliable control response, completed the pre-use check, and returned the ventilator to service.

helpfulDetails: Entire screen or localized area affected

title: Getinge Servo-air Ventilator - Turbine / Blower Fault or Insufficient Flow
description: Addresses inadequate airflow or turbine/blower-related symptoms caused by circuit restrictions, filters, setup, power, environmental conditions, or service-level faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient Immediately
steps.instructions: If delivered flow or ventilation is unreliable, move the patient to another verified ventilator or provide an appropriate alternate ventilation method before troubleshooting. Do not continue using a ventilator that cannot reliably meet commanded ventilation. Expected outcome: Patient ventilation is maintained independently of the affected Servo-air.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Operate the ventilator with an appropriate test load and determine whether the problem is low delivered flow, delayed pressure development, abnormal turbine sound, startup failure, or a displayed turbine/blower-related condition. Expected outcome: The symptom is reproduced under controlled conditions. If ventilation is normal and the symptom cannot be reproduced, continue with inspection and functional verification before return to service.

steps.title: 3. Verify AC Power and Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Connect the ventilator to a known-good AC outlet and confirm stable operation. Inspect the power cord and inlet externally. A low or unstable power condition can complicate blower performance assessment. Expected outcome: The ventilator has a stable power source. If performance normalizes on reliable AC power, evaluate the power/battery issue separately before return to service.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Patient Circuit for Restriction
steps.instructions: Inspect the entire circuit for: Kinked tubing Occluded connectors Water accumulation Incorrectly installed components Blocked filters Obstructed humidification components Pinched hoses Correct any obvious restriction. Expected outcome: The circuit has a clear, unrestricted gas path. If adequate flow returns after correcting the restriction, troubleshooting can stop after full performance verification.

steps.title: 5. Check External Filters and Air Path
steps.instructions: Inspect externally accessible air-intake areas and approved replaceable filters for visible blockage, contamination, or improper installation. Do not open the ventilator or access internal turbine components. Expected outcome: External air paths are unobstructed and filters are correctly installed and serviceable.

steps.title: 6. Simplify the Breathing System
steps.instructions: Temporarily use the simplest approved test circuit and remove unnecessary accessories that may introduce resistance. Use an appropriate test lung or simulator. Expected outcome: Flow and pressure delivery are normal with the simplified setup. Reintroduce external components one at a time if needed to identify the restriction.

steps.title: 7. Substitute Known-Good External Components
steps.instructions: Replace suspect filters, tubing, circuit components, or test accessories with known-good compatible items. Expected outcome: Normal ventilation is restored with a known-good external component. Replace the defective accessory and complete final testing.

steps.title: 8. Check Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify that vents are not blocked by bedding, packaging, wall placement, or equipment stacked against the ventilator. Confirm the ventilator has adequate clearance and is not exposed to obvious excessive heat, dust, or contamination. Expected outcome: The ventilator has an unobstructed external cooling and intake environment.

steps.title: 9. Perform Functional Verification
steps.instructions: With a verified circuit and test load, confirm stable startup, delivered ventilation, expected pressure and flow response, and normal alarm operation. Use approved test equipment when quantitative performance verification is required. Expected outcome: Ventilation is stable and consistent with configured settings. If verified, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Turbine or Flow Problems
steps.instructions: If insufficient flow, abnormal turbine operation, unusual noise, overheating, or repeatable turbine-related faults remain after external causes are eliminated, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The unit remains out of service for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Servo-air was producing insufficient flow during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a severely restricted external breathing-circuit filter.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the restricted filter, verified normal flow and ventilation with a test load, completed the pre-use check, and returned the ventilator to service.

helpfulDetails: Final pre-use and functional test results

title: Getinge Servo-air Lite Ventilator - Alarm Speaker or Audible Alarm Failure
description: Addresses absent, weak, distorted, or intermittent audible alarms caused by settings, obstruction, ambient conditions, or internal alarm-system faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Alarm Coverage
steps.instructions: A Servo-air Lite without reliable audible alarms should not remain in patient service. Provide another verified ventilator or establish an appropriate alternate alarm and ventilation arrangement before troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient safety does not rely on the questionable alarm speaker.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Audible Alarm Failure
steps.instructions: Create an approved controlled alarm condition and determine whether the audible alarm is absent, weak, distorted, or intermittent. Verify visual alarm indication separately. Expected outcome: The audible alarm problem is reproduced.

steps.title: 3. Verify Alarm Volume Settings
steps.instructions: Review normal user-accessible alarm-volume settings. Do not use restricted menus or configuration changes to bypass alarm requirements. Expected outcome: The alarm volume is configured appropriately. Correcting a normal setting that restores reliable audio resolves the issue after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Speaker Opening
steps.instructions: Check the external speaker area for labels, tape, debris, contamination, or fluid residue. Do not insert objects into the opening. Expected outcome: The speaker opening is unobstructed.

steps.title: 5. Test in a Controlled Environment
steps.instructions: Repeat the alarm test in a quiet bench area. Expected outcome: The alarm is clearly audible. If it remains weak or absent, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: 6. Perform a Normal Restart
steps.instructions: Power the ventilator down and restart normally after removing it from patient use. Repeat alarm testing. Expected outcome: Alarm output is normal and stable after startup.

steps.title: 7. Test Multiple Alarm Conditions
steps.instructions: Use safe controlled methods to produce more than one alarm condition and confirm consistent audible annunciation. Expected outcome: The alarm speaker functions reliably during repeated testing.

steps.title: 8. Observe for Intermittent Failure
steps.instructions: Operate the ventilator during a reasonable bench test period and repeat alarm activation. Expected outcome: No loss, fading, or distortion occurs.

steps.title: 9. Complete Functional and Pre-Use Verification
steps.instructions: Run required pre-use testing and confirm visual and audible alarms function throughout. Expected outcome: Alarm performance is consistently normal. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Alarm Audio Failure
steps.instructions: If audible alarms remain absent, weak, distorted, or intermittent, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator remains out of service for internal alarm-system evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that alarms appeared visually on the Servo-air Lite but the audible alarm could barely be heard.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found adhesive material partially obstructing the external speaker opening.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed the obstruction, verified strong and consistent audible alarms under multiple test conditions, completed the pre-use check, and returned the ventilator to service.

title: Getinge Servo-air Lite Ventilator - Battery Not Charging or Short Runtime
description: Addresses battery charging or runtime problems caused by AC supply, connection, battery seating, battery condition, storage, or internal charging faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Reliable Power
steps.instructions: Do not intentionally test questionable battery operation while a patient depends on the ventilator. Connect to reliable AC power and arrange alternate ventilation before battery troubleshooting. Expected outcome: Patient ventilation is protected from power interruption.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Battery Symptom
steps.instructions: Determine whether the battery is not recognized, does not charge, discharges quickly, or causes unexpected shutdown. Record battery and AC status indications. Expected outcome: The specific power complaint is identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify the AC Source
steps.instructions: Confirm the power cord is fully connected and the outlet is known good. Inspect the cord, plug, and external power inlet. Expected outcome: Reliable AC power is present. If charging resumes, continue verification before return to service.

steps.title: 4. Allow Appropriate Charging
steps.instructions: If the battery was deeply discharged or stored, allow a normal charging opportunity according to applicable manufacturer guidance. Expected outcome: Charge indication increases normally. No charging response warrants further troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Battery Condition
steps.instructions: Where permitted through normal handling, inspect the battery for swelling, leakage, cracks, contamination, damaged contacts, or improper seating. Expected outcome: The battery is physically safe and properly installed. Damaged batteries are removed from service.

steps.title: 6. Reseat the Battery
steps.instructions: Remove and reinstall the battery if allowed and while the ventilator is not supporting a patient. Expected outcome: The battery is recognized and begins charging normally.

steps.title: 7. Install a Known-Good Compatible Battery
steps.instructions: Use a known-good approved battery. Expected outcome: Normal charging with the substitute identifies the original battery as defective. Failure with both batteries suggests a ventilator charging-system problem.

steps.title: 8. Verify Runtime
steps.instructions: After sufficient charging, perform a controlled battery runtime evaluation under applicable department and manufacturer criteria. Expected outcome: Battery performance is acceptable and stable.

steps.title: 9. Verify AC-to-Battery Transition
steps.instructions: During controlled testing, confirm the ventilator transitions appropriately between AC and battery operation without reset or unexpected shutdown. Expected outcome: Backup power operates reliably. Troubleshooting can stop after successful verification.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Charging Problems
steps.instructions: If the Servo-air Lite will not charge or properly operate with a known-good battery and verified AC source, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator remains out of service for qualified power-system evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Servo-air Lite battery showed little runtime despite being connected to AC power.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the installed battery failed runtime testing while a known-good compatible battery operated normally.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the battery, verified normal charging and battery operation, completed functional testing, and returned the ventilator to service.

title: Getinge Servo-air Lite Ventilator - Expiratory Cassette Not Recognized or Not Seated
description: Addresses cassette recognition or seating problems caused by incomplete insertion, contamination, moisture, damage, incompatibility, or obstruction at the cassette interface.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: Do not remove or reseat the expiratory cassette while a patient depends on the ventilator. Transfer ventilation to another verified device or appropriate alternate method first. Expected outcome: Patient ventilation is safely maintained away from the affected unit.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Cassette Symptom
steps.instructions: Verify whether the cassette is physically difficult to seat, appears seated but is not recognized, or causes a pre-use check failure. Note the displayed condition. Expected outcome: The specific recognition or seating problem is confirmed.

steps.title: 3. Remove and Inspect the Cassette
steps.instructions: Inspect the cassette for cracks, warping, contamination, fluid, damaged interfaces, or other visible defects. Do not disassemble it beyond approved handling. Expected outcome: The cassette is physically suitable for use. Any visibly damaged cassette is removed from service.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Receptacle
steps.instructions: Inspect the external cassette receiving area for contamination, debris, fluid, or an obstruction. Do not probe or adjust internal contacts. Expected outcome: The receptacle is clean and unobstructed.

steps.title: 5. Reinstall the Cassette
steps.instructions: Align and install the cassette normally without unusual force. Expected outcome: The cassette seats completely and is recognized. If recognition returns, proceed to the complete pre-use check.

steps.title: 6. Confirm Compatibility and Proper Processing
steps.instructions: Verify the cassette is approved for the Servo-air Lite and has been cleaned, dried, and prepared according to applicable requirements. Expected outcome: A correct, properly prepared cassette is installed.

steps.title: 7. Substitute a Known-Good Cassette
steps.instructions: Use a known-good compatible cassette. Expected outcome: Recognition with the substitute identifies the original cassette as the cause. If neither cassette is recognized, escalate after confirming the receptacle is unobstructed.

steps.title: 8. Complete the Pre-Use Check
steps.instructions: Run the full required pre-use check. Expected outcome: The cassette remains recognized and all checks pass. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Verify Normal Ventilation
steps.instructions: Operate the ventilator with an appropriate test load and verify normal expiratory function and alarm behavior. Expected outcome: Ventilation is stable and no cassette-related fault recurs.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Recognition Failure
steps.instructions: If known-good cassettes are not recognized or do not seat normally, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The unit remains out of service for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Servo-air Lite would not recognize the installed expiratory cassette.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the cassette was not completely seated after reprocessing.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed and correctly reinstalled the cassette, confirmed recognition, completed the pre-use check successfully, and returned the ventilator to service.

title: Getinge Servo-air Lite Ventilator - High Airway Pressure Alarm
description: Addresses high-pressure alarms caused by circuit restriction, filters, water, expiratory obstruction, settings, accessories, or ventilator-related pressure-control problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient First
steps.instructions: Clinical staff should immediately assess the patient, airway, and ventilation when a high airway pressure alarm occurs. If effective ventilation is uncertain, move the patient to another verified ventilator or use an appropriate alternate ventilation method. Expected outcome: Patient ventilation is stabilized before equipment troubleshooting.

steps.title: 2. Reproduce the Condition on a Test Load
steps.instructions: After removing the ventilator from patient use, connect an appropriate test lung and determine whether the high-pressure alarm recurs. Expected outcome: The alarm is either confirmed as an equipment/setup issue or does not reproduce outside the clinical condition.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Circuit
steps.instructions: Check inspiratory and expiratory tubing for kinks, trapped water, blocked connectors, pinched tubing, caps, or incorrect assembly. Expected outcome: The breathing circuit is unobstructed. If correcting an obstruction resolves the alarm, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 4. Check Filters and Inline Accessories
steps.instructions: Inspect filters, HMEs, humidification components, adapters, and other accessories for restriction or incorrect installation. Expected outcome: All components permit normal gas flow. Replace any restricted accessory.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Expiratory Cassette
steps.instructions: Confirm the cassette is fully seated, correctly prepared, and free from obvious external obstruction or damage. Expected outcome: The expiratory path is externally normal.

steps.title: 6. Review Settings
steps.instructions: Review applicable pressure targets, pressure limits, PEEP, tidal volume, and alarm settings. Do not increase limits simply to eliminate an alarm. Expected outcome: Settings are appropriate for controlled bench testing and do not explain an expected high-pressure alarm.

steps.title: 7. Use a Known-Good Test Circuit
steps.instructions: Replace the circuit and external accessories with known-good compatible components. Expected outcome: The alarm disappears if an external circuit component was responsible.

steps.title: 8. Evaluate Pressure Response
steps.instructions: Observe pressure delivery with the test lung and use approved ventilator test equipment where required. Expected outcome: Pressure rises and stabilizes predictably. Uncommanded or excessive pressure requires removal from service.

steps.title: 9. Verify Alarm Performance
steps.instructions: Create a controlled high-pressure condition to confirm the alarm activates and clears appropriately after the test condition is removed. Expected outcome: High-pressure alarm operation is normal. Troubleshooting can stop after successful testing.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent High Pressure
steps.instructions: If excessive pressure or the alarm persists with an unrestricted known-good circuit and appropriate settings, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator remains out of service for qualified internal evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported recurrent high airway pressure alarms from the Servo-air Lite during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an occluded inline filter increasing breathing-circuit resistance.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the filter, verified normal pressure delivery and alarm operation with a test lung, completed the pre-use check, and returned the ventilator to service.

title: Getinge Servo-air Lite Ventilator - Network, Serial, or Data Communication Failure
description: Addresses communication loss caused by cables, external interfaces, infrastructure, ports, accessible configuration, or downstream monitoring and integration systems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Clinical Monitoring and Documentation
steps.instructions: If ventilator data is expected at a central monitoring system, EMR, or integration platform, confirm that staff have another method to monitor and document the patient while communication is unavailable. Expected outcome: Patient care continues safely without relying on missing remote data.

steps.title: 2. Define the Failed Communication Path
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves Ethernet, serial data, device integration, central monitoring, export, middleware, or intermittent communication. Confirm whether local Servo-air Lite ventilation and alarms remain normal. Expected outcome: The failed portion of the communication workflow is identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Communication Cables and Connectors
steps.instructions: Check Ethernet, serial, adapter, and interface cables for secure seating, visible damage, bent connectors, and strain. Reseat accessible connections. Expected outcome: Connections are secure. If communication returns and remains stable, proceed to end-to-end verification.

steps.title: 4. Observe Link and Status Indicators
steps.instructions: Check applicable port, network, interface-adapter, or downstream connection indicators. Compare with a nearby functioning setup when useful. Expected outcome: Physical link status is consistent with proper connectivity.

steps.title: 5. Substitute Known-Good External Hardware
steps.instructions: Replace the external communication cable with a known-good equivalent or connect to a verified infrastructure port when authorized. Expected outcome: Restored communication identifies a cable or port problem.

steps.title: 6. Verify Approved Accessible Configuration
steps.instructions: Review normal accessible network or serial configuration and compare it with the approved configuration for the location or a known-good device. Do not alter protected network parameters or service settings without authorization. Expected outcome: Configuration matches the intended communication environment.

steps.title: 7. Check External Infrastructure
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the bedside integration hardware, network switch, serial converter, device adapter, interface engine, server, or receiving application is functioning for other equipment. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to the ventilator or the surrounding infrastructure.

steps.title: 8. Verify End-to-End Data Reception
steps.instructions: After correction, verify that expected Servo-air Lite data appears at the actual destination system. Do not consider link lights alone sufficient. Expected outcome: Data is transmitted and received consistently. Troubleshooting can stop after successful end-to-end verification.

steps.title: 9. Verify Normal Ventilator Function
steps.instructions: Complete appropriate functional and pre-use testing to confirm that communication troubleshooting did not alter ventilator operation. Expected outcome: Local ventilation and alarms remain fully functional.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Unresolved Communication Failure
steps.instructions: If cables, ports, infrastructure, and approved configuration are verified but communication remains unavailable, escalate to qualified Clinical Engineering, IT, integration, or manufacturer support personnel. Expected outcome: The affected communication workflow remains out of service until the full path is restored and verified.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Servo-air Lite was ventilating normally but no data was appearing at the connected clinical information system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external Ethernet cable had a damaged connector and would not maintain network link.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the cable, verified stable network link and data at the receiving system, confirmed normal ventilator operation, and returned the device to service.

title: Getinge Servo-air Lite Ventilator - O2 Cell Calibration Failure or Incorrect FiO2
description: Addresses oxygen calibration or FiO2 discrepancies caused by oxygen supply, leaks, circuit setup, sensing components, configuration, or service-level oxygen-system faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: If oxygen concentration is uncertain, remove the Servo-air Lite from patient dependence and maintain ventilation and oxygen delivery with a verified alternate device. Expected outcome: The patient receives reliable oxygen independently of the affected ventilator.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Oxygen Discrepancy
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue is calibration failure, incorrect displayed FiO2, unstable readings, or mismatch between selected and delivered oxygen. Use an approved calibrated oxygen analyzer when appropriate. Expected outcome: The reported oxygen problem is confirmed independently where needed.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Oxygen Source
steps.instructions: Inspect the oxygen hose and fittings for secure connection, damage, kinks, or leakage. Verify the source is available using an appropriate external method. Expected outcome: A reliable oxygen source is connected.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Breathing Circuit
steps.instructions: Check for significant leaks, disconnected tubing, open ports, and incorrectly installed circuit components. Expected outcome: Circuit integrity is sufficient for reliable oxygen delivery and testing.

steps.title: 5. Verify Normal Accessible Settings
steps.instructions: Review the selected oxygen concentration and normal user-accessible settings. Do not change protected calibration values or enter unauthorized service menus. Expected outcome: The intended oxygen setting is correctly configured.

steps.title: 6. Perform Approved Oxygen Calibration
steps.instructions: With verified supply and circuit conditions, perform the normal approved calibration procedure. Expected outcome: Calibration completes successfully. If measured oxygen is then accurate and stable, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 7. Inspect Approved Replaceable Oxygen-Sensing Components
steps.instructions: If an oxygen-sensing component is designed for routine replacement, inspect it for physical deterioration, loose installation, contamination, or other obvious issues. Expected outcome: The component is correctly installed and serviceable.

steps.title: 8. Substitute a Known-Good Approved Component
steps.instructions: If applicable, install a known-good compatible oxygen-sensing component and repeat calibration. Expected outcome: Successful calibration identifies the original replaceable component as defective.

steps.title: 9. Verify Delivered Oxygen
steps.instructions: Operate the ventilator with an appropriate test setup and compare delivered oxygen with an approved analyzer. Expected outcome: Oxygen delivery and indication meet applicable acceptance requirements. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Oxygen Failure
steps.instructions: If calibration continues to fail or oxygen remains inaccurate after external causes are ruled out, discontinue troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The Servo-air Lite remains out of service for qualified oxygen-system evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Servo-air Lite failed oxygen calibration during preparation for use.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the oxygen supply hose was loosely connected and the source was not reaching the ventilator reliably.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the oxygen connection, completed calibration successfully, verified delivered oxygen with an approved analyzer, and returned the ventilator to service.

title: Getinge Servo-air Lite Ventilator - Patient Circuit Leak or Disconnection Alarm
description: Addresses leak or disconnect alarms caused by loose connections, damaged tubing, open ports, humidification components, accessories, or expiratory-system problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: If a leak or disconnect alarm occurs during patient ventilation, immediately verify the patient connection and actual ventilation. Provide another verified ventilator or alternate ventilation method if adequate support is uncertain. Expected outcome: Patient ventilation is reliable before Clinical Engineering troubleshooting begins.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Alarm
steps.instructions: Connect the Servo-air Lite to an appropriate test lung using the reported circuit configuration and reproduce the condition if possible. Expected outcome: The leak or disconnection alarm is confirmed under controlled conditions.

steps.title: 3. Trace All Circuit Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect every connection from the ventilator outlet through the patient circuit, humidifier, filters, adapters, and test lung. Reseat loose connections. Expected outcome: Connections are secure. If the alarm clears, complete final verification and stop troubleshooting when successful.

steps.title: 4. Check for Open Ports
steps.instructions: Inspect sampling ports, nebulizer ports, drain ports, accessory connections, and unused openings for missing caps or unintended openings. Expected outcome: No unintended open gas pathway remains.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Tubing and Connectors
steps.instructions: Look for cracks, punctures, loose cuffs, damaged connectors, or intermittent separation. Expected outcome: Tubing and connectors are intact. Damaged components are replaced.

steps.title: 6. Inspect Humidification Components
steps.instructions: Verify the chamber and associated connections are properly assembled and sealed. Expected outcome: Humidification components do not create an unintended leak.

steps.title: 7. Verify the Expiratory Cassette
steps.instructions: Confirm that the cassette is correctly seated and recognized. Expected outcome: The expiratory interface is properly installed and does not contribute to the leak condition.

steps.title: 8. Substitute a Known-Good Circuit
steps.instructions: Install a known-good compatible circuit and test lung. Expected outcome: If the alarm disappears, the original circuit or external accessory is the source.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Leak and Functional Testing
steps.instructions: Run the required circuit or pre-use checks and verify stable ventilation and proper disconnection alarm operation. Expected outcome: No unexpected leak alarm remains. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Leak Alarms
steps.instructions: If the alarm persists with a sealed known-good circuit and properly installed cassette, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator remains out of service for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported a continuous circuit leak alarm on the Servo-air Lite.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an unused accessory port on the patient circuit left open.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering correctly closed the port, completed the circuit and pre-use checks, verified ventilation and disconnect alarm operation, and returned the ventilator to service.

title: Getinge Servo-air Lite Ventilator - Pre-Use Check Failure
description: Addresses failed pre-use checks caused by circuit setup, expiratory cassette, accessories, oxygen supply, power, leaks, or other externally correctable conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Remove the Ventilator From Active Use
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot a Servo-air Lite pre-use failure while a patient depends on the ventilator. Transfer ventilation to another verified device or appropriate alternate ventilation method. Inspect for obvious physical damage, contamination, fluid intrusion, overheating, or unusual odor. Expected outcome: Patient care is protected and the ventilator is available for controlled troubleshooting. Visible damage requires removal from service.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Pre-Use Check Failure
steps.instructions: Repeat or review the pre-use check in a safe test environment and identify the exact stage that fails. Record any displayed message and whether the failure is repeatable. Expected outcome: The failed portion of the check is clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify AC Power and Startup
steps.instructions: Connect the Servo-air Lite to a known-good AC source and inspect the power cord and plug. Confirm the ventilator completes normal startup without resetting or displaying unrelated power issues. Expected outcome: Stable power is available. If proper power restores successful testing, complete the full check and stop troubleshooting when verified.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Patient Circuit
steps.instructions: Check tubing, connectors, filters, humidification components, accessory ports, test lung, and caps for correct assembly and obvious leaks or obstruction. Expected outcome: The test circuit is complete, secure, and correctly configured.

steps.title: 5. Inspect and Reseat the Expiratory Cassette
steps.instructions: Verify the cassette is compatible, properly prepared, undamaged, and fully seated. Remove and reinstall it using normal approved handling. Expected outcome: The cassette is recognized and securely seated. If the pre-use check passes, troubleshooting can stop after complete verification.

steps.title: 6. Verify Oxygen Supply if Required
steps.instructions: Inspect the oxygen hose, source, and external connections. Verify the source is available using an appropriate method. Expected outcome: Required oxygen supply is connected and available.
