steps.title: 7. Remove Nonessential Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect optional external accessories and repeat the check using the simplest approved configuration. Expected outcome: The check completes successfully in the basic configuration, indicating an external accessory or setup issue.

steps.title: 8. Use Known-Good External Components
steps.instructions: Substitute compatible known-good circuits, cassette, oxygen hose, test accessory, or other implicated external component one at a time. Expected outcome: The failed condition clears when the defective external component is removed.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Run the entire required pre-use check and verify ventilation into an appropriate test load, controls, and alarm operation. Expected outcome: The pre-use check passes completely and ventilation is stable. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate if the Check Still Fails
steps.instructions: If the same failure persists after external setup, supply, and accessory causes are ruled out, discontinue troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The Servo-air Lite remains out of service for qualified bench evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Servo-air Lite failed its pre-use check during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an incompletely connected breathing-circuit limb producing a leak.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the circuit connection, completed the pre-use check successfully, verified ventilation and alarms, and returned the ventilator to service.

title: Getinge Servo-air Lite Ventilator - Touchscreen or Control Input Unresponsive
description: Addresses unresponsive or intermittent controls caused by screen contamination, obstruction, power instability, startup state, external accessories, or control-system faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient
steps.instructions: If the Servo-air Lite cannot be reliably controlled, transfer the patient to another verified ventilator or appropriate alternate ventilation method. Expected outcome: Patient ventilation and alarm management do not depend on an unreliable interface.

steps.title: 2. Characterize the Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the entire screen is frozen, a portion is unresponsive, another control is affected, or the problem is intermittent. Observe whether displayed values and waveforms continue updating. Expected outcome: The control failure is clearly characterized.

steps.title: 3. Inspect and Clean the Interface
steps.instructions: Check for moisture, cleaning residue, tape, labels, protective material, physical damage, or objects contacting the screen. Clean and dry the exterior according to approved procedures. Expected outcome: The interface is clean and unobstructed. If normal response returns, continue functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify Stable AC Power
steps.instructions: Connect the ventilator to a known-good AC outlet and inspect the power cord. Expected outcome: The device operates from stable power without unexplained resets.

steps.title: 5. Perform a Normal Restart
steps.instructions: With the unit removed from patient use, perform a normal shutdown and restart. Do not use undocumented reset combinations or restricted service menus. Expected outcome: The touchscreen and controls initialize normally.

steps.title: 6. Remove Nonessential External Connections
steps.instructions: Disconnect optional network, serial, USB, and other external accessories not needed for basic operation. Expected outcome: Controls remain responsive in a simplified configuration.

steps.title: 7. Check the Full Accessible Touch Area
steps.instructions: Operate normal user-accessible screen controls and look for dead zones, delay, unintended activations, or intermittent response. Expected outcome: The full control interface responds consistently.

steps.title: 8. Verify Settings and Alarm Control
steps.instructions: Confirm that settings can be selected and changed appropriately during bench testing and that alarm acknowledgement controls work normally. Expected outcome: Essential ventilator control functions are reliable.

steps.title: 9. Complete Pre-Use Testing
steps.instructions: Run the required pre-use check and observe the interface throughout operation. Expected outcome: The interface remains responsive with no recurring freeze. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Control Failure
steps.instructions: If the display or controls remain intermittently or continuously unresponsive, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The Servo-air Lite remains out of service for qualified evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported intermittent touchscreen response on the Servo-air Lite during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found moisture and cleaning residue on the touchscreen surface.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering cleaned and dried the display using the approved method, verified consistent touchscreen and alarm-control response, completed the pre-use check, and returned the ventilator to service.

title: Getinge Servo-air Lite Ventilator - Turbine / Blower Fault or Insufficient Flow
description: Addresses inadequate airflow or turbine/blower symptoms caused by circuit restriction, filters, power, external airflow obstruction, accessories, or service-level faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient Immediately
steps.instructions: If the ventilator cannot reliably provide required flow or pressure, transfer the patient to another verified ventilator or appropriate alternate ventilation method. Expected outcome: Patient ventilation is maintained independently of the affected Servo-air Lite.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Test the ventilator with an appropriate test load and determine whether the complaint is insufficient flow, delayed pressure development, abnormal turbine sound, startup failure, or another blower-related symptom. Expected outcome: The condition is reproduced under controlled conditions.

steps.title: 3. Verify Stable Power
steps.instructions: Connect to a known-good AC source and verify normal power indications. Inspect the cord and plug externally. Expected outcome: Stable electrical power is available to the ventilator.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Breathing Circuit
steps.instructions: Check for kinked tubing, water accumulation, occluded connectors, blocked filters, pinched hoses, incorrect assembly, or obstructed humidification components. Expected outcome: The patient circuit is unrestricted. If normal flow returns after correcting an obstruction, troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 5. Inspect External Air Paths
steps.instructions: Check externally accessible intake areas and approved external filters for blockage or contamination. Ensure blankets, packaging, walls, or other equipment are not obstructing airflow around the ventilator. Expected outcome: Air intake and ventilation openings are clear.

steps.title: 6. Simplify the Test Configuration
steps.instructions: Use a known-good compatible circuit and test lung without unnecessary inline accessories. Expected outcome: Ventilation is normal in the simplified configuration. Reintroduce external accessories individually if necessary.

steps.title: 7. Substitute Suspect External Components
steps.instructions: Replace suspect tubing, filters, or circuit accessories with known-good compatible items. Expected outcome: Normal flow returns when the defective external component is removed.

steps.title: 8. Observe Turbine Operation
steps.instructions: Listen for abnormal mechanical sound and observe whether flow and pressure are stable. Do not open the ventilator or access internal turbine components. Expected outcome: Turbine operation sounds and behaves normally during testing.

steps.title: 9. Perform Performance Verification
steps.instructions: Use approved ventilator test equipment when quantitative verification is required and complete the required pre-use check. Expected outcome: Ventilation performance meets applicable acceptance criteria. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Turbine or Flow Problems
steps.instructions: If flow remains inadequate with a known-good unrestricted circuit and stable power, or abnormal turbine noise persists, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator remains out of service for qualified service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported low airflow from the Servo-air Lite during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a blocked external circuit filter restricting flow.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering replaced the filter, verified normal flow and pressure delivery with a test lung, completed the pre-use check, and returned the ventilator to service.
